title: Beating RL With Reflection: GEPA and Optimize Anything — Lakshya A. Agrawal, GEPA
talk_summary: GEPA is a reflective prompt/harness optimizer that runs a candidate on a few examples, collects rich textual feedback (errors, traces, domain info), has an LLM reflect and propose improved text artifacts, and keeps a Pareto pool of candidates that win on any example to avoid local optima. They show large gains from tiny sample counts versus RL, and generalize the method to optimize any text artifact (prompts, agent harness code, skills, scheduling policies) given a scoring function plus side information.

takeaways.technique: Reflective optimization of agent prompts/skills from traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the agent on a handful of real tasks, feed the full trace plus error messages and domain docs to an LLM reflector that proposes a revised prompt/skill, iterate with a Pareto pool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it runs reflection with an LLM or agent that reads the feedback and proposes a better prompt
takeaways.numbers: 2x GRPO gains with 3 data points vs 25,000 rollouts; NPU task 4.25%->30.52%; skills 24%->93% on GPT5-mini, transferred to Sonnet 4.5 at 100% with ~50% less time

takeaways.technique: Learn an LLM-judge from ~50 human-annotated traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Collect production traces, have a human annotate ~50 with detailed feedback, then optimize an LLM-as-judge prompt against those annotations and use it to drive further optimization.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Get a human to annotate just about 50 of those trajectories giving very detailed feedback

takeaways.technique: Optimize the agent harness file itself as text
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the whole agent harness (Python/JS) as a text artifact and run the same reflect-and-score loop to discover better control flow and tool orchestration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your entire agent harness is eventually just a Python or a JavaScript file and we can apply the same kind of reflective optimization
takeaways.numbers: 4-line program -> 6-step agent, Gemini Flash RAG 32.5%->89.5% in 16 rounds

takeaways.technique: Pareto candidate pool instead of greedy loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep every candidate that wins on even one training example rather than only the top scorer, avoiding local optima during search.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it keeps a parto pool where it keeps every single candidate that wins on even one training example and not just the top scorer
takeaways.numbers: >half of GEPA gains from Pareto selection; ~2x vs LLM-in-a-loop

takeaways.technique: Distill expensive-model behavior into cheap-model prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Optimize prompts/skills on a cheap model, then transfer the learned text artifact to stronger models, gaining both accuracy and speed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: skills that were optimized very cheaply on a GPT5 mini agent we are able to take that and apply to the latest claude sonnet
takeaways.numbers: GPT-4.1-mini prompt beat GPT-4.1 on math; Databricks 90x cost reduction, GPT-OSS-120B outperforming Opus

takeaways.technique: Feed actionable side information to the reflector
takeaways.what_they_do: Return compiler errors, profiler output, tool-call errors, and docs as an open-ended dict alongside the score so the optimizer learns domain specifics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If your domain produces compiler error messages, profiler messages, tool call error messages, return that
